---
title: Kumo
description: Install the independent Kumo theme, configure runtime light and dark modes, and understand compatibility and distribution.
---

Kumo is an optional appearance for Tile UI, maintained in `@tile-ui/theme-kumo`. It changes visual values, not the component implementation. Its only visual source is SCSS, compiled directly to CSS; React, Vue, and Solid consume the same stylesheet.

## Package installation

Install the independent theme package with `pnpm add @tile-ui/theme-kumo`. Shared component styles remain in `@tile-ui/styles`. The theme is authored in SCSS and exports only CSS/Sass; it has no JavaScript token API.

Choose the global appearance at build time by importing Kumo **instead of** the default theme or globals entry:

```tsx title="src/app.tsx"
import '@tile-ui/theme-kumo/theme.css';
import '@tile-ui/styles/reset.css'; // Optional; omit if your application already has a reset.
```

For a Sass pipeline, replace the CSS import with `import '@tile-ui/theme-kumo/theme.scss'`. Kumo includes Tile extension defaults and Kumo light/dark tokens, not the default palette or reset. A separate tokens import is unnecessary. Do not combine Kumo with `theme.*` or `globals.*`: globals loads Tile's default palette, not a theme-neutral base.

Toggle `.light`/`.dark` or `data-theme="light"`/`data-theme="dark"` on `html` at runtime; keep the markers consistent if using both. No theme provider, `data-tile-theme` attribute, or dynamic stylesheet swap is required. Resolve system preference in your existing application mode manager and update the root marker, so body-level portals inherit the same mode.

Tile component prop names and defaults remain unchanged; the complete Kumo variant/component API is not mirrored. Fonts are not fetched automatically: load any desired fonts through local assets or your own font setup. `createThemeVariables` and `applyThemeVariables` from `@tile-ui/core` still produce Tile default concrete values, so do not call them for Kumo class/attribute mode toggles; inline values can override the selected stylesheet.

This is a Kumo-derived appearance, not verified pixel parity or a complete accessibility audit. The default-palette contrast figures in the general theming guide do not validate Kumo contrast.

### Charts and Liveline

SVG Chart reads CSS variables; an explicit per-mode color in its config still takes priority. Liveline with an omitted `theme` inherits the stylesheet's `--tile-color-mode` marker (Kumo sets light/dark). Without that marker it preserves the legacy dark default. Explicit `theme="light"` or `theme="dark"` always wins; there is no new `"auto"` value. Root mode changes repaint an existing Liveline canvas without recreating it.

## Registry installation

UI items depend on `@tile-ui/styles`, which copies Sass support files and injects only Tile extension defaults; the host still owns the semantic palette. Keep the optional `@tile-ui/theme-default` item for Tile's default palette, or choose Kumo explicitly:

```bash
pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @tile-ui/theme-kumo
```

The Kumo item depends on `@tile-ui/styles` and copies `styles/themes/kumo.scss`, the `_shared.scss`, `_light.scss`, and `_dark.scss` partials, and `styles/themes/LICENSE.kumo` (retain this MIT license and Cloudflare notice). It does not inject Kumo `cssVars`, import itself, or swap the host theme automatically. Explicitly import the copied `styles/themes/kumo.scss` once from your root entry with the appropriate local path. Do not import the theme partials separately, and remove default-theme/globals imports and conflicting host palette declarations when adopting Kumo.

## Runtime mode switching and first paint

Use a single root marker convention. For example, application-side browser code can update the attribute without loading another stylesheet:

```js
document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme', 'dark');
document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme', 'light');
```

Light is the default. Resolve system preference with your application's mode manager and apply the resolved root marker before first paint where possible. Keep server markup and client hydration consistent. Persistence and system-preference listeners are application concerns, not part of the theme package.

Apply the marker to `html` so body-level portals inherit it. Explicit light/dark resets are provided, but arbitrary nested themes are not a compatibility guarantee.

## Customization and scope

Override semantic and component CSS custom properties in an application stylesheet after the theme. The theme covers palette, dimensions, typography, borders, shadows, state styling, and visual motion; it does not copy component CSS or add behavior. For example:

```css
:root {
  --tile-font-sans: 'Avenir Next', sans-serif;
  --tile-button-height: 2.5rem;
}
```

Use existing Tile component APIs for composition and interaction. Any missing state, structure, measurement, or drawing capability must be supplied as a generic framework interface, not theme JavaScript.

## Compatibility and validation limits

Card, Tooltip, Skeleton, Spinner, Calendar, and chart rendering retain Tile's structure and engines, so some upstream visual differences remain. The theme does not promise complete upstream component or variant parity. Chromium checks cover selected states and mode switching, not every browser or a complete accessibility audit.

Accessibility corrections intentionally differ from the reference: light link text is darker, dark links use the semantic text-link value, inactive light Tabs use a higher-contrast neutral, and keyboard focus rings are retained. Verify your own overrides and content for contrast and focus visibility.

## Source and license

The reference is [Cloudflare Kumo](https://github.com/cloudflare/kumo/tree/7e0ff40546f08405d05bc9754f0ff0fd009ece0a), pinned to `7e0ff40546f08405d05bc9754f0ff0fd009ece0a`. The theme package's `LICENSE` contains the complete upstream MIT notice. Preserve that file when redistributing the theme; registry installation carries it as `styles/themes/LICENSE.kumo`.
